summary:
Technical review of phase:rework-6, iteration 1 (sub-mv47spzw-01781921; handoff ho-mv47ltf3-01c9351a; decision dec-mv46ovt6-01a662af; commit 223780a). Run run-mv47te5g-0126322e.

**Scope and hashes.** The three artifacts match the submitted sha256 (submission 8cefaaa2, uploads-retention 295bb790, planner-sec-b1 95a40b59). `git diff --stat 66206c9 223780a` touches only the two test files. g1 (0a57aea) landed frontend files while I reviewed; it does not touch either test file, src/domain, or src/services/retention.js. I re-ran every check I cite on the current tree (28de3ab8). My earlier runs on the submitted tree 622af87f had the same results; they are listed in the C-checks notes and are not cited, because the tree has changed since.

**FU-33 is fixed and the test is not weakened.**
- I reproduced the race: the pre-rework test fails on a 300 ms delayed-unlink mutant.
- The revised test passes on that mutant.
- The revised test fails at the new bounded wait (L718), with its message, when the swept file is never removed.
- Full npm test under the lock is green: 2307 tests, 2299 pass, 0 fail, 8 skipped.
- **FU-33's close rule is met.** Locked green runs on the fixed test: ev-mv47hp51, ev-mv47qjdl, my ev-mv47y0fp-01c51970 (on 622af87f, the third), ev-mv48e1xg (frontend-engineer) and my ev-mv48mk97-01920d24. There was no red run in between.

**FU-46 meets its own resolution text.** Every exactness assertion is kept, the p95 stays at 20 ms, and a generous ceiling is added. Real algorithmic regressions remain killed: the full-enumeration mutants by PLANNER_LIMIT (engineer's evidence); my no-lower-bound mutant with the cap raised 20x by the 1000 ms ceiling alone. Five other single-cut mutants do not change timing under either the old or the new test.

**What is lost (TR-R6-1, minor).** My mutant pl-delay is exact and never throws, but holds the event loop for 300 ms (the SEC-B-1 symptom) on 49 inputs. It survives the revised file, and the pre-rework per-call bounds kill it. I name a noise-robust assertion that would catch it.

**Other findings.** Two minor/info traceability items, and info notes on the disclosures. None of them blocks. Decision: approve.

criteria.description: Rework: FU-33 (TR-F-7) retention test waits for the file; FU-46 SEC-B-1 per-call bound robust to host noise; a regression test fails before the fix and passes after; the existing checks still pass
criteria.notes:
**FU-33.**
- **Fails before, passes after.** The pre-rework test (66206c9) fails on my mutant ur-delay, where the unlink starts 300 ms after the row is gone: 41 tests, 40 pass, 1 fail, at the immediate file check, expected false, actual true (ev:ev-mv48ndz6-01faec70, a check that passes only on that failure). The revised test passes on the same mutant, 41/41 (ev:ev-mv48nmfy-0138988b).
- **Not weakened.** On my mutant ur-never, the timer-tick image's file is removed neither by the sweep nor by the orphan sweep. The revised test fails exactly at L718, with 'the file of the swept image is unlinked within 5 s of its row going' (kill-check ev:ev-mv48nwxf-019ae428). The poll at L714-L717 only delays the assertion; it cannot turn a file that is still present into a pass.
- **Real tree.** The file alone passes 41/41 (ev:ev-mv48mvw7-01ebcdb0).

**FU-46.**
- **Exactness kept in all three tests.** No call may throw (L57, L82, L121). The A-only plan, its lines, total, pickups and maxPickups-1 equality are kept, and so are `calls == 1008`, `20 < feasible < 150` and the p95 < 20 ms (L93).
- **The ceiling is chosen from measurements** (L12-L24).
- **Kills.** The engineer's full-enumeration mutants are killed by PLANNER_LIMIT (ev:ev-mv47dqfe-018e0d01, ev:ev-mv47dsj8-0120cf95; their diffs are in scratchpad/rework6/pl-*/mutant.diff and I checked them). My pl-nolb-cap mutant (exact, never throws) is killed by the 1000 ms ceiling alone: catalog 35 took 1328 ms (ev:ev-mv48p2md-01f16a78).
- **Real tree.** The file alone passes 3/3 (ev:ev-mv48mxa9-01f0afee).
- The lost per-call sensitivity is recorded as TR-R6-1 (minor).

**Existing checks.** npm test under the lock passes: 2307 / 2299 / 0 fail / 8 skipped (ev:ev-mv48mk97-01920d24).

criteria.description: The retention behaviour the test asserts matches the spec, and the no-unlink survivor does not hide a defect
criteria.notes:
**The spec.** L773: 'The hourly sweep deletes rows and files ... and writes an image.retention_delete audit event per image. Startup also removes orphan files older than 1 day.' L979: 'orphan files, and an audit row per deletion'.

**Why the engineer's first no-unlink mutant passes** (ev:ev-mv476e0b-01cc6895):
- the orphan step of the same pass removes the file, with its own image.orphan_delete audit row;
- so the file and the row are gone and every deletion has an audit row, as the spec requires;
- the outcome is spec-conformant and hides no product defect.

**Its survival depends on the date.** The orphan age check (retention.js L79) compares the pinned clock, FIXED_NOW_MS 2026-10-20T06:00Z (app-harness L24), with the file's real mtime. After 2026-10-19T06:00Z wall-clock time, a freshly written file is not 'older than 1 day' by that clock, and the same mutant would die at L718.

The gap in attribution is pre-existing. It is recorded as TR-R6-4 (info).

findings.title: SEC-B-1 lost its per-call latency sensitivity below 1 s: an exact, non-throwing mutant that holds the event loop 300 ms on 49 inputs passes the revised test
findings.detail:
**What SEC-B-1 was about.** rev-mv1ijr52-01b2f4b6 raised it with two harms: PLANNER_LIMIT on fillable requests, and 'holds the event loop up to about 0.3 s'.
- The first harm is still pinned exactly.
- The second was pinned by the per-call bounds: 50 ms for test 1, 100 ms for each sweep call, 250 ms for each 12-offer catalog. All three are now 1000 ms (L63, L84, L124).
- The only aggregate bound left is the sweep p95, and it is blind to any slowdown that affects up to 5 % of the 1,008 calls. Test 3 has no aggregate bound at all.

**The survivor.** Mutant pl-delay (scratchpad/tr-r6/pl-delay/mutant.diff, printed first in each log):
- planner.js busy-waits 300 ms when cups >= 10,000, maxPickups is 5 and every offer holds 100-200 bundles;
- that is 48 sweep calls (4.8 %) plus the stock-100 / 10,000-cup headline call;
- the results stay exact and nothing throws.
- **The revised file passes it, 3/3** (ev:ev-mv48owz8-014723b9, exit 0 = survives). Test 2 takes 14.9 s instead of about 0.3 s.
- **The pre-rework file kills it** on exactly the removed bounds, 'took 301.1 ms' in test 1 and 'took 301.6 ms' in test 2 (kill-check ev:ev-mv48oyj8-01600f49).

**Why it is minor, not blocking.**
1. FU-46 itself prescribes 'the p95 plus a generous per-call ceiling', and that is what was built and disclosed (disclosures 1 and 2).
2. Real algorithmic regressions are still killed:
   - full enumeration, by PLANNER_LIMIT (engineer);
   - no lower bound, by PLANNER_LIMIT at the 2M cap (7 catalogs throw, ev:ev-mv48pr50-01e290e5);
   - no lower bound with the cap at 40M, by the ceiling alone (ev:ev-mv48p2md-01f16a78).
   The other five single-cut mutants (no dominance table, no irredundancy cut, no subset mandatory cut, no incumbent break, no subset root bound) do not change timing under either test. The worst is pl-noroot at 216 ms on a 12-offer catalog, which is under the old 250 ms too (ev:ev-mv48pr50-01e290e5).
3. What slips is an input-targeted hold of 0.1-1 s, which a pure planner is unlikely to acquire.
4. The old bounds were a recorded source of red full runs (186.9 ms, 327.9 ms).

The residual is still real for the security reading of SEC-B-1: an attacker picks one input, and a p95 does not protect a single input.
findings.recommendation:
Owner: test-engineer, through phase G or the next rework that owns test/timing/** (the orchestrator routes it).

**Fix: re-time on exceed.** When a call exceeds its pre-rework bound (50 ms test 1, 100 ms sweep, 250 ms 12-offer), call plan() on the same input twice more and fail only if the MINIMUM of the three timings is still above the bound. Keep the 1000 ms ceiling on the first timing as the runaway guard.
- Host contention and steal are transient and do not repeat three times on one input. A deterministic hold does.
- This needs no new constant.
- As an alternative or addition, give test 3 a p95 bound over its 150 catalogs.

**Resolved when:**
- the revised test fails on pl-delay (scratchpad/tr-r6/pl-delay/mutant.diff), shown by a kill-check that passes only on that failure;
- the file stays green 3/3 under the same 3 x nproc CPU-contention runs as ev:ev-mv47feek-01fdb68f;
- one locked npm test is green.

**Alternative:** an orchestrator decision accepts a per-call hold of up to 1 s as a SEC-B-1 residual, alongside SEC-B-1R / RISK-19, and the verification report lists it.

findings.title: uploads-retention L711-L713 attribute to 'spec: Retention' a sentence that is the source comment at src/services/retention.js L35
findings.detail:
The comment quotes 'row and audit event first; an unlink that fails leaves an orphan for the orphan sweep' as 'spec: Retention'.
- That wording is not in spec.md.
- It paraphrases retention.js L35: 'Row and audit event first: if the file cannot be unlinked it is an orphan, and the orphan sweep removes it later.'
- The spec says only that the sweep deletes rows and files with an audit event per image, and that startup removes orphan files older than 1 day (L773, L979).

The behaviour and the fix are unaffected; only the traceability is wrong. This is the same kind as TR-R5-2 (minor), and the delivery-lead disclosed it (disclosure 4).
findings.recommendation:
Owner: whoever next owns test/api/uploads-retention.test.js (test-engineer). It can be folded into the TR-R6-1 or TR-R6-4 change.

Resolved when the comment cites src/services/retention.js L35 for the ordering, and spec 'Retention and deletion' (L773) only for what that section says.

findings.title: Disclosure 2's 'no mutant can show the ceiling alone firing' is inaccurate: an exact, non-throwing mutant is killed by the 1000 ms ceiling alone
findings.detail:
**The ceiling fires.** Mutant pl-nolb-cap removes the node lower-bound cut and raises the node cap from 2M to 40M. It never throws, and the revised test fails only at test 3: 'catalog 35 took 1328.0 ms (runaway ceiling 1000 ms ...)' (kill-check ev:ev-mv48p2md-01f16a78).

**What stays true.**
- The p95 line is still not shown firing by any mutant.
- With the same cut and the 2M cap, 7 of the 150 catalogs throw PLANNER_LIMIT, so exactness kills that variant (ev:ev-mv48pr50-01e290e5).

This corrects the record in the test's favour; it is not a defect.
findings.recommendation:
No change to the tests.

Resolved when the verification report states FU-46's coverage as: exactness (PLANNER_LIMIT) plus the ceiling, both shown firing by a mutant; the p95 not shown firing.

findings.title: No RS-39 test attributes a swept image's unlink to the image step; the no-unlink mutant survives through the orphan step, and only while the wall clock is before 2026-10-19
findings.detail:
**Why the engineer's first no-unlink mutant passes** (ev:ev-mv476e0b-01cc6895).
- The orphan step of the same pass unlinks the file and writes image.orphan_delete. The outcome is spec-conformant (L773, L979), so this is not a product defect.
- Survival needs the orphan age check (retention.js L79) to see the fresh file as older than 1 day, measured against the pinned clock (FIXED_NOW_MS 2026-10-20T06:00Z, app-harness L24).
- From 2026-10-19T06:00Z wall-clock time, the same mutant would be killed at L718.

**Pre-existing gap.** No test pins that the image step itself unlinks. The 7 d + 1 min test checks only that the file is gone. The gap is not introduced by rework-6, and the rework's new wait is not weakened by it: my ur-never kill-check is red at L718 (ev:ev-mv48nwxf-019ae428).
findings.recommendation:
Optional, for the next owner of uploads-retention.test.js. In the 'kept at 6 days 23 hours, deleted at 7 days + 1 minute' test, assert `swept.imageFilesLeft === 0` and that no image.orphan_delete event names the swept file.

Resolved when the engineer's one-line no-unlink mutant (shown in the log of ev:ev-mv476e0b-01cc6895) fails that test whatever the wall-clock date, shown by a kill-check. Otherwise, close it as accepted in the verification report.

findings.title: Disclosures 5 and 6 accepted: one scratch directory reused (both diffs recoverable from their logs); the 20-run loop log shows exit codes, not counts
findings.detail:
**Disclosure 5, the directory reuse.**
- ur-nounlink/mutant.diff now holds only the extended version.
- I checked both logs: ev:ev-mv476e0b-01cc6895 prints the one-line `leftForOrphanSweep += 1` diff, with 33/33 pass; ev:ev-mv476u2l-01edbb7b prints that line plus the orphan-sweep `continue`, with 30/33.
- Both versions are recoverable. The one-directory-per-mutant rule (TR-R5-4) was broken once; nothing was lost.

**Disclosure 6, the loop log.**
- ev:ev-mv47lom9-015c619a stops at the first non-zero exit, and node --test exits non-zero on any failing or cancelled test. The 20 'run N ok' lines therefore prove 20 clean runs.
- The command has no name filter, so each run executed the whole file. Only the per-run counts are missing.
- My own locked runs supersede the loop for FU-33 in any case.
findings.recommendation:
No change for this gate. For later loops, print each run's '# tests/# pass/# fail' lines (for example `| grep -E '^# (tests|pass|fail)'`) instead of discarding the TAP, and never reuse a mutant directory.

Resolved going forward when the next mutant or loop evidence follows this.
